overview: This Senate resolution designates October 26, 2026, as the "Day of the Deployed," a day the Senate has recognized each year since 2011. It honors members of the U.S. armed forces who are deployed away from home, including National Guard and Reserve members, noting that more than 2 million service members have deployed to the Middle East region since the September 11, 2001, attacks. It also recognizes the sacrifices made by military families and the U.S. commitment to easing service members' return home. The resolution asks Americans to reflect on deployed troops' service and to mark the day with ceremonies and activities. The Senate approved it by unanimous consent on September 29, 2026.
for: Supporters say the day gives Americans a chance to recognize service members serving far from home and the families who wait for them.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic: it does not change any law or provide new funding or new benefits for deployed troops or their families.
